Please solve this issue: TitleCleanupJob strips the stray quotes the legacy exporter wrapped around
every leaf title. It runs for hours here and deploys keep interrupting it, and
every restart starts over at the first leaf. So early titles get cleaned twice
— titles that legitimately open with a quoted phrase are getting mangled — and
the tail of the collection never gets done.

Make it resumable: after an interruption it picks up where it left off,
redoing at most the leaf it was on, so every title ends up cleaned exactly
once with its inner quotes intact.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  # = Active Job Continuable
  #
  # The Continuable module provides the ability to track the progress of your
  # jobs, and continue from where they left off if interrupted.
  #
  # Mix ActiveJob::Continuable into your job to enable continuations.
  #
  # See {ActiveJob::Continuation}[rdoc-ref:ActiveJob::Continuation] for usage.
  #
  module Continuable
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      class_attribute :max_resumptions, instance_writer: false
      class_attribute :resume_options, instance_writer: false, default: { wait: 5.seconds }
      class_attribute :resume_errors_after_advancing, instance_writer: false, default: true

      around_perform :continue

      def initialize(...)
        super(...)
        self.resumptions = 0
        self.continuation = Continuation.new(self, {})
      end
    end

    # The number of times the job has been resumed.
    attr_accessor :resumptions

    attr_accessor :continuation # :nodoc:

    # Start a new continuation step
    def step(step_name, start: nil, isolated: false, &block)
      unless block_given?
        step_method = method(step_name)

        raise ArgumentError, "Step method '#{step_name}' must accept 0 or 1 arguments" if step_method.arity > 1

        if step_method.parameters.any? { |type, name| type == :key || type == :keyreq }
          raise ArgumentError, "Step method '#{step_name}' must not accept keyword arguments"
        end

        block = step_method.arity == 0 ? -> (_) { step_method.call } : step_method
      end
      checkpoint! if continuation.advanced?
      continuation.step(step_name, start: start, isolated: isolated, &block)
    end

    def serialize # :nodoc:
      super.merge("continuation" => continuation.to_h, "resumptions" => resumptions)
    end

    def deserialize(job_data) # :nodoc:
      super
      self.continuation = Continuation.new(self, job_data.fetch("continuation", {}))
      self.resumptions = job_data.fetch("resumptions", 0)
    end

    def checkpoint! # :nodoc:
      interrupt!(reason: :stopping) if queue_adapter.stopping?
    end

    def interrupt!(reason:) # :nodoc:
      instrument :interrupt, reason: reason, **continuation.instrumentation
      raise Continuation::Interrupt, "Interrupted #{continuation.description} (#{reason})"
    end

    private
      def continue(&block)
        if continuation.started?
          self.resumptions += 1
          instrument :resume, **continuation.instrumentation
        end

        block.call
      rescue Continuation::Interrupt => e
        resume_job(e)
      rescue Continuation::Error
        raise
      rescue StandardError => e
        if resume_errors_after_advancing? && continuation.advanced?
          resume_job(exception: e)
        else
          raise
        end
      end

      def resume_job(exception) # :nodoc:
        executions_for(exception)
        if max_resumptions.nil? || resumptions < max_resumptions
          retry_job(**self.resume_options)
        else
          raise Continuation::ResumeLimitError, "Job was resumed a maximum of #{max_resumptions} times"
        end
      end
  end

  ActiveSupport.run_load_hooks(:active_job_continuable, Continuable)
end

      def performed_jobs
        @performed_jobs ||= []

        perform_or_enqueue(perform_enqueued_jobs && !filtered?(job), job, job_data)

        job_data = job_to_hash(job, at: timestamp)

            job_data[:priority] = job_data.fetch("priority")

module ActiveJob
  class Continuation
    module Validation # :nodoc:
      private
        def validate_step!(name)
          validate_step_symbol!(name)
          validate_step_not_encountered!(name)
          validate_step_not_nested!(name)
          validate_step_resume_expected!(name)
          validate_step_expected_order!(name)
        end

        def validate_step_symbol!(name)
          unless name.is_a?(Symbol)
            raise_step_error! "Step '#{name}' must be a Symbol, found '#{name.class}'"
          end
        end

        def validate_step_not_encountered!(name)
          if encountered.include?(name)
            raise_step_error! "Step '#{name}' has already been encountered"
          end
        end

        def validate_step_not_nested!(name)
          if running_step?
            raise_step_error! "Step '#{name}' is nested inside step '#{current.name}'"
          end
        end

        def validate_step_resume_expected!(name)
          if current && current.name != name && !completed?(name)
            raise_step_error! "Step '#{name}' found, expected to resume from '#{current.name}'"
          end
        end

        def validate_step_expected_order!(name)
          if completed.size > encountered.size && completed[encountered.size] != name
            raise_step_error! "Step '#{name}' found, expected to see '#{completed[encountered.size]}'"
          end
        end

        def raise_step_error!(message)
          raise InvalidStepError, message
        end
    end
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  class Continuation
    # = Active Job Continuation Step
    #
    # Represents a step within a continuable job.
    #
    # When a step is completed, it is recorded in the job's continuation state.
    # If the job is interrupted, it will be resumed from after the last completed step.
    #
    # Steps also have an optional cursor that can be used to track progress within the step.
    # If a job is interrupted during a step, the cursor will be saved and passed back when
    # the job is resumed.
    #
    # It is the responsibility of the code in the step to use the cursor correctly to resume
    # from where it left off.
    class Step
      # The name of the step.
      attr_reader :name

      # The cursor for the step.
      attr_reader :cursor

      def initialize(name, cursor, job:, resumed:)
        @name = name.to_sym
        @initial_cursor = cursor
        @cursor = cursor
        @resumed = resumed
        @job = job
      end

      # Check if the job should be interrupted, and if so raise an Interrupt exception.
      # The job will be requeued for retry.
      def checkpoint!
        job.checkpoint!
      end

      # Set the cursor and interrupt the job if necessary.
      def set!(cursor)
        @cursor = cursor
        checkpoint!
      end

      # Advance the cursor from the current or supplied value
      #
      # The cursor will be advanced by calling the +succ+ method on the cursor.
      # An UnadvanceableCursorError error will be raised if the cursor does not implement +succ+.
      def advance!(from: nil)
        from = cursor if from.nil?

        begin

require 'resque/worker'

class Resque::Pool
  module PooledWorker
    attr_accessor :pool_master_pid
    attr_accessor :worker_parent_pid

    # We will return false if there are no potential_parent_pids, because that
    # means we aren't even running inside resque-pool.
    #
    # We can't just check if we've been re-parented to PID 1 (init) because we
    # want to support docker (which will make the pool master PID 1).
    #
    # We also check the worker_parent_pid, because resque-multi-jobs-fork calls
    # Worker#shutdown? from inside the worker child process.
    def pool_master_has_gone_away?
      pids = potential_parent_pids
      pids.any? && !pids.include?(Process.ppid)
    end

    def potential_parent_pids
      [pool_master_pid, worker_parent_pid].compact
    end

    def shutdown_with_pool?
      shutdown_without_pool? || pool_master_has_gone_away?
    end

    def self.included(base)
      base.instance_eval do
        alias_method :shutdown_without_pool?, :shutdown?
        alias_method :shutdown?, :shutdown_with_pool?
      end
    end

  end
end

    def sanitize_for_index(text)

        text

        Rails::Html::FullSanitizer.new.sanitize(text)
      end
    end

steps.reasoning_content:
**Deep Dive into Resumable Title Cleanup**

Alright, let's break this down. The core issue is a long-running job, `TitleCleanupJob`, that strips quotes from leaf titles. The current implementation restarts from the beginning on interruption, leading to duplicate cleaning of early titles and never completing the entire set. The goal is to make it resumable, picking up where it left off, and ensuring that each title is cleaned exactly once without mangling inner quotes. This sounds fairly straightforward, but the devil, as always, is in the details.

First, I looked at the basic code: a `find_each` loop applying a simple `delete_prefix` and `delete_suffix`. Naively adding `ActiveJob::Continuable` seems like a start, using the `step` feature. However, I immediately recognized the need for rigorous checking.

My first alarm bell was regarding ActiveJob's `resume_options` and Resque. The default `wait` of 5 seconds will throw an `NotImplementedError` unless `resque-scheduler` is present. And it's not present! This means our automatic retries won't be scheduled, leading to immediate failures on interruption. We *must* consider how to handle this critical setup issue. Either we add the gem, or we ensure `resume_options = {}` to avoid scheduling.

Next, I shifted my focus to the graceful shutdown of the Resque workers, especially on deploy. How is `queue_adapter.stopping?` handled in Resque and ActiveJob? Tracing signals from the container's `SIGTERM` through `bin/boot`, `Procfile`, and `resque-pool`, I saw some red flags. `resque-pool` defaults to an immediate shutdown, signaling `TERM` to workers. But does `Resque::Worker` correctly handle `TERM` when `FORK_PER_JOB=false`? No. The worker sets `@shutdown = true` and the workers continue until they finish the current job or are SIGKILL'd. The key thing here is how `shutdown` is handled. If the job runs a long time, the worker may not react quickly enough to shutdown. This means that if we are not careful about `checkpoint!` calls, some jobs will not be interrupted, and may run again on restart, cleaning some titles more than once. We NEED to call `checkpoint!` within the cleanup loop to ensure that jobs are interrupted.

Then, there's the core logic of the cleanup itself and its interaction with the "redo at most the leaf it was on" requirement. The key here is to truly understand the impact of the `cleaned` method on titles with legitimately quoted phrases, like `"Hello" World`. Double cleaning this will strip that inner quote, thus corrupting data.

Now, let's look at the continuation logic when using `step`:

-   A graceful interruption will happen if `stopping?` is `true`, and it will throw a `Continuation::Interrupt`. The job will be re-enqueued using `retry_job`, and continue where it left off.
-   If an exception occurs within `leaf.update!`, then if `resume_errors_after_advancing?` is `true`, the job also gets re-enqueued, and it picks up from the same leaf.
-   But if the process gets SIGKILL'd *after* a leaf is updated, but *before* the continuation state is saved to the queue, all progress will be lost. The process, when it runs again, does not know the work it has done, or the leaf it was working on.

This is the central point: the *state* of the current leaf and the cursor *must* be saved either:
1.  in the database
2.  in Redis
before we can set `@cursor`.

Because otherwise, the title can be mangled, or cleaned more than once. It is this condition that we must address.

I need to confirm the SIGKILL behavior. Can we use the database to save a "checkpoint" before the `advance!` call? Can we store data in Redis? This is the major issue.

require "active_support/rescuable"

module ActiveJob
  # = Active Job \Execution
  #
  # Provides methods to execute jobs immediately, and wraps job execution so
  # that exceptions configured with
  # {rescue_from}[rdoc-ref:ActiveSupport::Rescuable::ClassMethods#rescue_from]
  # are handled.
  module Execution
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern
    include ActiveSupport::Rescuable

    # Includes methods for executing and performing jobs instantly.
    module ClassMethods
      # Performs the job immediately.
      #
      #   MyJob.perform_now("mike")
      #
      def perform_now(...)
        job_or_instantiate(...).perform_now
      end

      def execute(job_data) # :nodoc:
        ActiveJob::Callbacks.run_callbacks(:execute) do
          job = deserialize(job_data)
          job.perform_now
        end
      end
    end

    # Performs the job immediately. The job is not sent to the queuing adapter
    # but directly executed by blocking the execution of others until it's finished.
    # +perform_now+ returns the value of your job's +perform+ method.
    #
    #   class MyJob < ActiveJob::Base
    #     def perform
    #       "Hello World!"
    #     end
    #   end
    #
    #   puts MyJob.new(*args).perform_now # => "Hello World!"
    def perform_now
      # Guard against jobs that were persisted before we started counting executions by zeroing out nil counters
      self.executions = (executions || 0) + 1

      deserialize_arguments_if_needed

      _perform_job
    rescue Exception => exception
      handled = rescue_with_handler(exception)
      return handled if handled

      run_after_discard_procs(exception)
      raise
    end

    def perform(*)
      fail NotImplementedError
    end

    private
      def _perform_job
        ActiveSupport::ExecutionContext[:job] = self
        run_callbacks :perform do
          perform(*arguments)
        end
      end
  end
end

      end

      def using_test_adapter?
        queue_adapter.is_a?(ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::TestAdapter)
      end

      def clear_enqueued_jobs
        enqueued_jobs.clear if using_test_adapter?
      end

      def clear_performed_jobs
        performed_jobs.clear if using_test_adapter?
      end

      def jobs_with(jobs, only: nil, except: nil, queue: nil, at: nil)
        validate_option(only: only, except: except)

        jobs.dup.select do |job|
          job_class = job.fetch(:job)

          if only
            next false unless filter_as_proc(only).call(job)
          elsif except
            next false if filter_as_proc(except).call(job)

steps.reasoning_content:
**Deep Dive into Resumable Title Cleanup**

Alright, let's break this down. First, the outer transaction test fixture being non-joinable is good news for `ActiveRecord.all_open_transactions`. Now, let's get serious and meticulously examine *every* potential problem in this system, starting from the ground up.

The core issue: a long-running job, `TitleCleanupJob`, is getting interrupted by deploys. This job, designed to strip stray quotes from titles, restarts from the beginning each time, leading to redundant work and an incomplete process. The goal is to make it resumable, preserving cleaned titles and finishing the job exactly once, even during interruptions.

Okay, let's dig into each piece:

### Layer A: The Job Itself (`app/jobs/title_cleanup_job.rb`)

This job is straightforward, `Leaf.find_each` and update titles. The interesting part is that `gem "rails", github: "rails/rails"` is Rails 8.2 with `ActiveJob::Continuable`, and the original app used Resque (before Solid Queue), which is now being used again with `resque-pool`, but without `resque-scheduler`!

**BIG RED FLAG:** We're mixing `ActiveJob::Continuable` with Resque. Here's where it can break badly.

---

### Trap 1: `ActiveJob::Continuable` and the `step` Loop

The current implementation uses `step` with `cursor` and `find_each`. We need to carefully trace what happens during interruptions.

1.  **First Run:** The `cursor` starts as `nil`. `Leaf.find_each(start: nil)` correctly starts from the lowest ID. As the job loops, `step.advance!` is called after each update, incrementing the `cursor`. If it interrupts before the first leaf, no problem. If an interruption occurs *after* a leaf is updated, then the next run uses the saved cursor to start where it left off.
2.  **Resumed Run:** The job is deserialized, `cursor` is restored. The `find_each` uses the saved cursor to restart. It correctly skips any leaves already updated.
3.  **Edge Case 1A:** If `queue_adapter.stopping?` is `true` *before* the first leaf, or at the start of the resumed job, no problem. It correctly interrupts and retries.
4.  **Edge Case 1B:** If an exception happens *during* `leaf.update!`, it rolls back the DB update. If `resume_errors_after_advancing?` is true and the job *had* advanced the cursor, the job will correctly restart from the correct place. However, if the error happens between a DB commit and the `step.advance!` step, we'll have duplicate work or a lost record.

---

### Trap 2: Resque and Deploy Interruptions

Here's the critical piece, especially without `resque-scheduler`!

**Thing 2A: `ResqueAdapter#enqueue_at` vs. `ActiveJob::Continuable.resume_options`!!**

Remember, `resume_options` defaults to `{ wait: 5.seconds }`. Here is the problem: when `checkpoint!` is called, `retry_job` uses `resume_options`. However, when using the Resque adapter without `resque-scheduler`, Resque does **NOT** support scheduled jobs. So, when the job tries to reschedule itself using `ResqueAdapter#enqueue_at`, it throws a **`NotImplementedError`**. THIS IS A SHOW STOPPER!! The job will crash, and all progress is lost.

If `resume_options` is an empty hash, `{}` (or has `wait: nil`), the job uses `enqueue`. This works, but we may get duplicate work when the adapter is Resque!

Let's test this in code.

**Analyzing ActiveJob's Retry and Resume Mechanism**

Okay, so I'm looking closely at this `structured_event_subscriber.rb` file, specifically line 118: `wait_seconds: wait.to_i`. The `nil.to_i` operation there is completely harmless; it evaluates to `0`, which is as expected. All good so far!

But hang on… I need to dig deeper. I'm going back to `ActiveJob::Core#set`. I'm seeing this:

  self
end

The heart of the matter seems to be around how `resume_options` are handled. I'm considering scenarios where `resume_options` is either empty (`resume_options = {}`) or explicitly set to `wait: nil` (`resume_options = { wait: nil }`). The `retry_job(**{})` call ends up calling `enqueue({})`, which then calls `set({})`. What happens then? The crucial line is `self.scheduled_at = options[:wait].seconds.from_now if options[:wait]`.

In both cases, `options[:wait]` is falsy (either because the key isn't present or because its value is `nil`), so `self.scheduled_at` becomes `nil`. That means, the job is enqueued immediately via `queue_adapter.enqueue(self)` instead of being scheduled using `queue_adapter.enqueue_at(self, timestamp)`.

The next thought is, what happens if the job *already* has a `scheduled_at` time, perhaps from an earlier scheduling with `wait:`? With the `TestAdapter` (and this is important), `enqueue_at` works fine. And, even better, if `scheduled_at` was originally set, the `retry_job` function saves and restores `scheduled_at`, so calling `enqueue({})` would *still* use the original `scheduled_at` from `deserialize` (and that would be a past timestamp). In fact, with `TestAdapter`, a past timestamp on `scheduled_at` would *still* be enqueued with `enqueue_at`. However, with `ResqueAdapter`, a job *can't* have `scheduled_at` because `ResqueAdapter#enqueue_at` is not implemented!

Even better still, `{ wait: nil }` and `{}` end up behaving *identically* in `set(options)` because the `if options[:wait]` condition is falsy for both. So, `self.resume_options = {}` (or `{ wait: nil }`) is perfectly safe and idiomatic!

Just to be absolutely certain, I should really grep the entire Rails codebase for usages of `resume_options` to confirm any conventions being used there. It is good to have some context!

    #
    # The adapter uses a {Concurrent Ruby}[https://github.com/ruby-concurrency/concurrent-ruby] thread pool to schedule and execute

    # short-lived jobs. Fine for dev/test; bad for production.
    class AsyncAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      # See {Concurrent::ThreadPoolExecutor}[https://ruby-concurrency.github.io/concurrent-ruby/master/Concurrent/ThreadPoolExecutor.html] for executor options.
      def initialize(**executor_options)
        @scheduler = Scheduler.new(**executor_options)
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        @scheduler.enqueue JobWrapper.new(job), queue_name: job.queue_name
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        @scheduler.enqueue_at JobWrapper.new(job), timestamp, queue_name: job.queue_name
      end

      # Gracefully stop processing jobs. Finishes in-progress work and handles
      # any new jobs following the executor's fallback policy (`caller_runs`).
      # Waits for termination by default. Pass `wait: false` to continue.
      def shutdown(wait: true) # :nodoc:
        @scheduler.shutdown wait: wait
      end

      # Used for our test suite.
      def immediate=(immediate) # :nodoc:
        @scheduler.immediate = immediate
      end

      # Note that we don't actually need to serialize the jobs since we're
      # performing them in-process, but we do so anyway for parity with other
      # adapters and deployment environments. Otherwise, serialization bugs
      # may creep in undetected.
      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        def initialize(job)
          job.provider_job_id = SecureRandom.uuid
          @job_data = job.serialize
        end

        def perform
          Base.execute @job_data
        end
      end

      class Scheduler # :nodoc:
        DEFAULT_EXECUTOR_OPTIONS = {
          min_threads:     0,
          max_threads:     ENV.fetch("RAILS_MAX_THREADS", 5).to_i,
          auto_terminate:  true,
          idletime:        60, # 1 minute
          max_queue:       0, # unlimited
          fallback_policy: :caller_runs # shouldn't matter -- 0 max queue
        }.freeze

        attr_accessor :immediate

          @immediate_executor = Concurrent::ImmediateExecutor.new
          @async_executor = Concurrent::ThreadPoolExecutor.new(
            name: "ActiveJob-async-scheduler",
            **DEFAULT_EXECUTOR_OPTIONS,
            **options
          )
        end

        def enqueue(job, queue_name:)
          executor.post(job, &:perform)
        end

        def enqueue_at(job, timestamp, queue_name:)
          delay = timestamp - Time.current.to_f
          if !immediate && delay > 0
            Concurrent::ScheduledTask.execute(delay, args: [job], executor: executor, &:perform)
          else
            enqueue(job, queue_name: queue_name)
          end
        end

        def shutdown(wait: true)
          @async_executor.shutdown
          @async_executor.wait_for_termination if wait
        end

          immediate ? @immediate_executor : @async_executor
        end

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

      define_method :positioning_parent do
        send(parent)
      end

      define_method :all_positioned_siblings do
        positioning_parent.send(association).send(filter).positioned
      end

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do
        all_positioned_siblings.excluding(self)
      end

      private :positioning_parent, :all_positioned_siblings, :other_positioned_siblings
    end
  end

  def previous
    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

  def move_to_position(offset, followed_by: [])
    with_positioning_lock do
      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)
      gap = (after - before) / (all_to_move.count + 1)

      all_to_move.each.with_index(1) do |item, index|
        item.update!(position_score: before + (index * gap))
      end

      remember_to_rebalance_positions if gap < REBALANCE_THRESHOLD
    end
  end

  def position_as_percentage
    100 * ordinal_position.to_f / all_positioned_siblings.count
  end

  private
    def ordinal_position
      other_positioned_siblings.before(self).count + 1
    end

    def insert_at_default_position
      with_positioning_lock do
        position_at_end
        yield
      end
    end

    def position_at_start
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)) - ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def position_at_end
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score) || 0) + ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def before_and_after_for(offset:, moving:)
      other_items = all_positioned_siblings.excluding(moving)

      if offset < 1
        after = all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)
        before = after - ELEMENT_GAP
      else

        before ||= all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score)
        after ||= before + (moving.count.succ * ELEMENT_GAP)
      end

    end

    def rebalance_required?

    end

module ActionText
  module HasMarkdown
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    class_methods do
      def has_markdown(name, strict_loading: strict_loading_by_default)
        class_eval <<-CODE, __FILE__, __LINE__ + 1
          def #{name}
            markdown_#{name} || build_markdown_#{name}
          end

          def #{name}?
            markdown_#{name}.present?
          end

          def #{name}=(content)
            self.#{name}.content = content

module ActiveStorage::Sluggable

  included do
    before_create :set_slug
  end

  def slug_path
    Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.action_text_markdown_upload_path(slug)
  end

  private
    def set_slug
      self.slug = "#{slug_basename}-#{SecureRandom.alphanumeric(6)}.#{slug_extension}"

    def slug_basename
      File.basename(slug_filename, ".*").parameterize
    end

    def slug_extension
      File.extname(slug_filename).delete(".").parameterize
    end

    def slug_filename
      slug.presence || filename.to_s

cat <<'EOF' > app/jobs/title_cleanup_job.rb
class TitleCleanupJob < ApplicationJob
  include ActiveJob::Continuable

  self.resume_options = {}

  rescue_from Resque::TermException do |exception|
    resume_job(exception)
  end

  def perform
    step :clean_titles do |step|
      Leaf.find_each(start: step.cursor, order: :asc) do |leaf|
        leaf.update!(title: cleaned(leaf.title))
        step.advance! from: leaf.id
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def cleaned(title)
      title.delete_prefix('"').delete_suffix('"')
    end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > config/initializers/resque.rb
module ResqueWorkerStopping
  def perform(job, &block)
    previous = Thread.current[:resque_worker]
    Thread.current[:resque_worker] = self
    super
  ensure
    Thread.current[:resque_worker] = previous
  end
end

module ResqueAdapterStopping
  def stopping?
    super || !!Thread.current[:resque_worker]&.shutdown?
  end
end

Resque::Worker.prepend ResqueWorkerStopping

ActiveSupport.on_load :active_job do
  require "active_job/queue_adapters/resque_adapter"
  ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::ResqueAdapter.prepend ResqueAdapterStopping
end
EOF

    @ordered_leaves[0].update!(title: '""Hello" World"')
    @ordered_leaves[1].update!(title: '""Quoted Title""')

    assert_equal '"Quoted Title"', @ordered_leaves[1].reload.title
    assert_equal "Plain Title", @ordered_leaves[2].reload.title
    assert_equal 'Say "Goodbye"', @ordered_leaves[3].reload.title

      perform_enqueued_jobs

**Red-Team Thinking: Breaking the Resumable Job!**

Okay, first things first: that initial test result, finding an unexpected job enqueued during `Leaf.destroy_all`, was a good catch! The `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob` triggered by destroying a `Picture` attached to a `Leaf` is expected. Now, let's make sure that's not just a fluke! The real focus is on the *resumable* aspect of `TitleCleanupJob`. The core of the problem it is solving is a common problem in long-running jobs.

We need to make sure the job picks up where it left off! I need to ensure that the code handles all forms of "interruption and resumption" correctly! The tests passed on the first run, but we can't be complacent. I'm going to put on my "red-team" hat and try to break my own code!

**Red-Team Question 1: What if the Job Dies Hard?**

What happens if a worker process gets brutally killed (`SIGKILL`), or an unhandled exception crashes the job and it restarts from scratch, bypassing the re-enqueued continuation payload? What if an `ActiveRecord::after_update_commit` callback raises an error *after* a database commit?

We need to test all the ways a test suite simulates an interruption, to see if they break the logic! My analysis is that we need a test for when a database commit has already happened, but `step.advance!` hasn't been called yet. We need a test for the case when there is an error in an `after_update_commit` callback, like `update_in_search_index`. That case can cause duplicate cleaning, and mangled titles! It turns out that this is an unavoidable at-least-once semantic of `ActiveJob::Continuable` because it is difficult to advance the cursor inside the same database transaction.

**Red-Team Question 2: Queue Adapter Shenanigans**

There is also the question about `TitleCleanupJob.queue_adapter`. Did setting `TitleCleanupJob.queue_adapter = adapter` define `_queue_adapter` on `TitleCleanupJob`, and not reset it to `nil` when `original_adapter` was `nil`? We need to make sure there is no state leakage between tests.

**Red-Team Question 3: Production Shutdowns**

We must simulate a `Resque::Worker#shutdown` in a production environment and ensure everything is behaving as expected. Let's trace every single line of production boot & deploy, including how `resque-pool` loads the Rails app.

**My Deep Dive into Resque Pool's Graceful Shutdown**

Alright, let's break this down. *Resque Pool* is fascinating, and I think I've just traced a very neat sequence.  Essentially, it's a carefully orchestrated dance of signals and checks, and I've got to understand how it works during a graceful shutdown, especially as it relates to my current problem and how continuations are handled.

It starts with the `Rakefile`, which, cleverly, loads the Rails environment through `config/application.rb`. This kicks off the whole shebang. Crucially, the Rails environment is preloaded via `resque:preload`, which means both `config/initializers/resque.rb` and `config/environments/production.rb` are loaded. This is important as it sets up eager loading and uses `resque` as the queue adapter through `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :resque`.

Now, here's where things get interesting.  `config/initializers/resque.rb` is run immediately.  `Resque::Worker.prepend ResqueWorkerStopping` happens *right away*.  And, simultaneously, `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_job` runs and prepends `ResqueAdapterStopping` to `ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::ResqueAdapter`.  This is our early warning system and shutdown hook.

When the `resque-pool` process receives a `SIGTERM` from `bin/boot`, the graceful shutdown begins.  The pool knows it's time to behave, specifically using the `graceful_worker_shutdown_and_wait` method.  It then sends a `SIGQUIT` to each Resque worker and waits, utilizing `reap_all_workers(0)`.

Each Resque worker, in turn, catches `SIGQUIT`.  This triggers the worker to call `worker.shutdown`, setting the `@shutdown` flag to `true`.  Perfect. Now the workers begin gracefully finishing their jobs.

Here's where my "aha!" moment happens. The `TitleCleanupJob` finishes its work updating the current leaf, it then calls `step.advance! from: leaf.id`.  This updates `step.cursor` and calls `checkpoint!`.  This is the critical path!  `checkpoint!` then calls `queue_adapter.stopping?`, which triggers the chain reaction:  `ResqueAdapterStopping#stopping?`... which checks `Thread.current[:resque_worker]&.shutdown? == true`.  This is a brilliant touch - checking if the worker is in shutdown mode!

Because `shutdown?` is `true`, an `ActiveJob::Continuation::Interrupt` is raised. This is the crucial signal to gracefully stop, and `ActiveJob::Continuable#continue` rescues this, calls `resume_job(e)` which then calls `retry_job(**{})`.  No `NotImplementedError` which is great!  It then re-enqueues the job using `ResqueAdapter#enqueue(self)`.  It's fascinating that `Resque.enqueue_to` is used. This allows the continuation and retry to happen. The job that is now serialized into Redis now correctly has `"continuation" => { "completed" => [], "current" => ["clean_titles", leaf.id + 1] }`.  This means the job is saved and can be resumed.

The `TitleCleanupJob#perform_now` then returns cleanly.  And then `Resque::Worker#work_one_job` calls `done_working`, loops and breaks, thanks to the `shutdown?` check.  The worker then exits cleanly, and finally, `resque-pool` reaps the worker and exits cleanly! Everything is as expected.

  private
    def with_failing_leaf_update(target_id, error)
      original = Leaf.instance_method(:update!)
      failed = false

      Leaf.define_method(:update!) do |*args, **kwargs|
        if !failed && id == target_id
          failed = true
          raise error
        end
        original.bind_call(self, *args, **kwargs)
      end

      yield
    ensure
      Leaf.define_method(:update!, original)
    end

    def with_after_leaf_update(target_id, callback)
      original = Leaf.instance_method(:update!)

      Leaf.define_method(:update!) do |*args, **kwargs|
        result = original.bind_call(self, *args, **kwargs)
        callback.call if id == target_id
        result
      end

      yield
    ensure
      Leaf.define_method(:update!, original)
    end

    def with_resque_adapter(adapter, enqueued)
      original_adapter = TitleCleanupJob._queue_adapter
      original_adapter_name = TitleCleanupJob._queue_adapter_name
      original_enqueue_to = Resque.method(:enqueue_to)

      TitleCleanupJob.disable_test_adapter
      TitleCleanupJob.queue_adapter = adapter
      Resque.define_singleton_method(:enqueue_to) do |queue, klass, *args|
        enqueued << [ queue, klass, args ]
      end

      yield
    ensure
      Resque.define_singleton_method(:enqueue_to, original_enqueue_to)
      TitleCleanupJob._queue_adapter = original_adapter
      TitleCleanupJob._queue_adapter_name = original_adapter_name
      TitleCleanupJob.enable_test_adapter(queue_adapter)
    end
end
